question: What validation and enforcement contract should govern prompt-bearing Markdown, and which decisions belong in OpenClaw core versus ClawHub?
rationale: Rule scope, warning-versus-block severity, trusted-local overrides, false-positive handling, and registry ownership change security posture and compatibility; source inspection cannot safely choose those product policies.

options.title: Shared contract, split ownership
options.body: Define one result schema and rule taxonomy in core, enforce it at model-visible ingestion points, and let ClawHub own publish-time scan state, tagging, and appeals.

options.title: ClawHub-only enforcement
options.body: Keep core loading behavior unchanged and limit mandatory validation to ClawHub publishing and verification, leaving local prompt files operator-trusted.

options.title: Guidance only
options.body: Document prompt-bearing Markdown risks and rely on sandboxing, tool policy, approvals, and operator review without adding a validator.

recommendation.title: Shared contract, split ownership
recommendation.body: Define one result schema and rule taxonomy in core, enforce it at model-visible ingestion points, and let ClawHub own publish-time scan state, tagging, and appeals.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already scoped the unresolved cross-surface decision and has recent history in the central prompt and workspace paths.
